mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in the Federal Funds rate above the 5-year moving average coincides with a negative 20-day S&P 500 forward return due to higher discount rates eroding expected equity payoffs.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS crosses above its 5-period SMA by at least 0.25 percentage points in the same month.
failure_condition: Over a 60-day window, 20-day forward returns remain positive despite trigger activation, or the 5-period SMA is not clearly below FEDFUNDS at the trigger point.

mechanism_narrative: When unemployment falls below 4.0% for two consecutive months, labor market strength supports corporate earnings expectations, driving a positive 60-day S&P 500 forward return.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE < 4.0 and UNRATE in month t-1 >= 4.0
failure_condition: In 20 out of 60 windows where the trigger occurs, the 20-day forward return is not statistically higher than the prior 20-day average (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A consecutive monthly decline in industrial production of at least 2% followed by a rebound above trend predicts a positive 20-day S&P 500 forward return as a contrarian reversal signal.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO falls 2% in month t, then INDPRO in month t+1 exceeds its 12-month moving average.
failure_condition: The 20-day forward return is negative in 4 or more of the next 10 such reversal windows.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly rise in consumer price index (CPIAUCSL) above 2% for three consecutive months indicates accelerating inflation, which compresses real equity valuations and produces a negative 5-day S&P 500 forward return.
failure_condition: Over 20 days following the trigger, 5-day forward returns remain non-negative in more than 70% of instances.

mechanism_narrative: When the ratio of residential housing starts (HOUST) to prior month is above 1.1 for two consecutive months, it signals a housing recovery that supports optimism in equities, yielding a positive 20-day forward return.
failure_condition: The 20-day forward return is not statistically different from zero (p > 0.05) in 8 out of 10 such windows.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp drop in monthly payroll employment (PAYEMS) of at least 50,000 jobs followed by a sustained rise of 100,000 jobs over the next two months predicts a positive 60-day S&P 500 forward return as a labor market recovery signal.
failure_condition: The 60-day forward return is negative in all 5 such recovery windows identified in the evidence window.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous decline in both unemployment (UNRATE) and industrial production (INDPRO) by at least 0.2 percentage points and 1% respectively in the same month indicates dual weakening demand-supply conditions that precede a negative 20-day S&P 500 forward return.
failure_condition: In 8 out of 12 windows with this interaction, the 20-day forward return is not significantly negative (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: During a period of monetary tightening (FEDFUNDS > 4.5%) but still low inflation (CPIAUCSL < 250), the S&P 500 tends to underperform in the near term due to rate-sensitive uncertainty, producing a negative 20-day forward return.
failure_condition: Over 30 windows matching the regime, the 20-day forward return is positive in more than 40% of instances.
